requirements.name: Relevant degree or demonstrated equivalent

lines.quote: Thesis: Spectral analysis methods for electroencephalography artifact rejection.

requirements.note: Degree is MSc Biomedical Engineering, not among the requirement's named fields; status reflects the 'demonstrated equivalent competence' alternative based on the quoted thesis and the peer-reviewed publication on spectral-filtering methods -- a judgement call for the recruiter under the refuse-to-guess rule.

lines.quote: Published a peer-reviewed conference paper at the Nordic Biomedical Engineering Symposium (NBEC 2016) on adaptive spectral filtering methods for EEG muscle-artifact rejection, based on my master's thesis work at Tammerkoski University.

Contributed a spectral-analysis module to an open-source MATLAB toolbox for biosignal processing. The module implements Welch's method with configurable windowing and overlap, and includes unit tests and user documentation.

requirements.note: Read as evidencing EU work authorisation via Finnish (EU) citizenship; the text does not itself use the words 'work authorisation'.

lines.quote: The company's working language is English, and all technical documentation, design reviews, and customer communications are conducted in English.
I am already in Oulu, already settled, and there are no logistical barriers.

ask_in_screening.question: Can you describe any experience you have designing or implementing phased-array or beamforming signal-processing algorithms?
Can you describe any experience you have writing embedded signal-processing software in C or C++ that runs on real hardware under real-time constraints?
Can you describe any experience you have writing Python to production or engineering standards, as opposed to one-off analysis scripts?
Can you describe any hands-on RF test-bench experience you may have, such as with network analysers, spectrum analysers, or anechoic-chamber measurement?
